title: Quality Characteristics for Testing (ISO 25010)
concept:
**ISO/IEC 25010** defines a product quality model with eight characteristics. Each can be the target of one or more test types.

**Functional suitability** — does the product provide the right functions correctly and appropriately? Sub-characteristics: functional completeness, correctness, appropriateness.

**Performance efficiency** — time behaviour, resource utilisation, capacity. Tested with load tests, stress tests, spike tests.

**Compatibility** — co-existence with other products, interoperability with other systems.

**Usability** — appropriateness recognisability, learnability, operability, user error protection, accessibility, aesthetic UI.

**Reliability** — maturity, availability, fault tolerance, recoverability. Tested with long-duration runs, fault injection, recovery scenarios.

**Security** — confidentiality, integrity, non-repudiation, accountability, authenticity. Tested with penetration tests, security scans, threat modelling exercises.

**Maintainability** — modularity, reusability, analysability, modifiability, testability.

**Portability** — adaptability, installability, replaceability.

Functional testing covers functional suitability; everything else is non-functional. The model gives teams a vocabulary for talking about quality and ensures they don't overlook a characteristic by accident.
keyPoints: ISO/IEC 25010 names 8 quality characteristics: functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, usability, reliability, security, maintainability, portability.
Functional suitability maps to functional testing; the other seven map to non-functional testing.
The model serves as a checklist so teams cover all relevant quality characteristics in their test plan.

quiz.question: A test verifies that a web application is readable by screen readers and conforms to WCAG 2.1 AA. Which ISO 25010 quality characteristic does this test PRIMARILY address?
quiz.explanation: Accessibility (screen reader support, WCAG conformance) is a sub-characteristic of usability in ISO/IEC 25010. Reliability is about availability and fault tolerance; functional suitability is about correctness of functions; portability is about installability/adaptability across environments.
